core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case using that both completion constructions commute with etale localisation (proof lines 8317-8320).

In the affine case with the closed subspace given by an ideal, show that when the ideal is finitely generated both completions equal the formal spectrum of the adic completion, citing the two corresponding affine statements (proof lines 8320-8326).

Construct the counterexample to the general assertion: for the polynomial ring in countably many variables and the ideal generated by them, exhibit a morphism which factors through the completion along the underlying closed subset but not through the completion along the closed subspace (proof lines 8326-8327).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the affine case (proof lines 8317-8320).
The finitely generated case: both completions are the same formal spectrum (proof lines 8320-8326).
difficulty_reason: For a closed subspace Z of an algebraic space X with underlying closed subset T, the lemma asserts that the canonical morphism from the completion along Z to the completion along T is an isomorphism when the inclusion is of finite presentation, and exhibits a case where it is not (statement lines 8308-8315). The proof first reduces to the affine case, because both constructions commute with etale localisation (proof lines 8317-8320). In the affine case, writing the closed subspace as the vanishing locus of an ideal, it observes that when that ideal is finitely generated both completions are the formal spectrum of the same adic completion, by the two comparison statements for affine formal completions; this gives the positive assertion (proof lines 8320-8326). It then constructs the counterexample to the general assertion: for the polynomial ring in countably many variables over the integers and the ideal generated by the variables, a morphism from the spectrum of the quotient by the ideals generated by the nth powers factors through the completion along the closed subset but not through the completion along the closed subspace, so the comparison morphism is not an isomorphism (proof lines 8326-8327). The claim is H3: the card carries both a positive argument resting on an identification of two completions and an explicit counterexample whose verification requires choosing the right ideal and exhibiting a morphism that distinguishes the two completions.
